newsitem.title: USA: Tech sector to make, break U.S. expansion--report.
newsitem.headline: Tech sector to make, break U.S. expansion--report.

text.p: Information and technology have replaced housing and auto manufacturing as the sectors that will determine how long the U.S. economic expansion lasts, according to Business Week magazine.
"There is a new business cycle, tied to the health of the high-tech sector," the cover story of the magazine's March 31 issue said.
Any slowdown on the sector's part would have repercussions throughout the rest of the economy, it said.
The story said the software, computer and information industries had grown at a pace far exceeding the pace of the rest of the economy.
"Over the past year, a stunning 33 percent of GDP growth has come from information-technology industries," it said.
The story said those industries had consequently replaced traditional cyclical indicators like automobile sales and housing starts to give warnings of an impending recession.

"There are some signs that such a high-tech slowdown may already have started," it said. "For one thing, tech stocks...are down 15 percent since mid-January. For another, demand for high-tech equipment is weakening."
